cause.kind: wall-clock assumption in the test, not a product race
cause.statement: The fixture target reads /mounted/input, prints it, and spins. The test gave it a 1 s execution timeout. The supervisor measures that deadline from its own start (supervisor_unix.go: deadline := startedAt.Add(ExecutionTimeout)) and sends SIGTERM 150 ms before it (50 ms cleanup reserve plus the 100 ms terminate grace), so the target had 850 ms of host time to be launched through the supervisor and bootstrap processes, read, and print. Under CPU load the watchdog fired first.
cause.retained_output: red-failing-output.txt: WatchdogTimeout:true, Signal:"terminated", Stdout empty, IOROMounts Requests:0 (the target had not asked for its input)
cause.same_cause_at_three_lines: line 22 is the fixture; lines 33 and 47 (old numbering) are the two real-executor replays, which read the same 1 s limit from the manifest

fix: The fixture and the two real-executor replays repeat a run whose watchdog fired before the target wrote output, under the next of 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32 s. The manifest records the timeout the fixture used. No assertion changed.

residual.what: At 64 load processes on 8 CPUs, 1 of 20 runs of the new test failed with a different signature: execution.Run returned an untyped error because the supervisor did not deliver its started and final reports inside the 1 s deadline. The old test makes the same call with the same deadline, so this is not introduced here; it was not seen in the old test's 100 runs. It did not occur in 200 runs at 16 and 32 load processes.
residual.why_not_handled: The error carries no type, so the test could only repeat on any error or match its text, and either would hide a real execution failure. Separating 'the deadline passed before the supervisor finished' from other protocol failures is a product change in runner/internal/execution.
